data.name: Ayodhya
data.gender_notes: Ayodhya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayodhya is the name of a legendary city in Hindu mythology, known as the capital of the ancient Raghav Dynasty ruled by King Rama. The name Ayodhya is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Ayus’ which means ‘life’ and ‘Dhya’ which means ‘that which is not perishable or indestructible’. Thus, Ayodhya is a symbol of immortality and indestructibility.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the eternal and indestructible nature of the soul.
data.etymology: Ayodhya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Imperishable, Indestructible.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayodhya total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Ayodhya is a significant cultural symbol and is celebrated in numerous Hindu texts and epics, most notably the Ramayana. It is believed that Lord Rama, the prince of Ayodhya, lived here before his exile and eventual defeat of the demon king, Ravana. The city is known to have influenced the arts, literature, and architecture. The significance of Ayodhya as a cultural icon can be seen in the numerous temples, structures, and monuments dedicated to Lord Rama and the Raghav Dynasty.
data.spiritual_significance: Ayodhya holds immense spiritual significance for Hindus as it is believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama, the embodiment of Dharma (righteousness) and an ideal role model of human conduct. The story of Rama’s life, as depicted in the Ramayana, has become a source of moral guidance and spiritual inspiration for millions of Hindus across the world. Ayodhya is also considered to be a tirtha (a sacred place) that offers spiritual merit and blessings to pilgrims who visit the city. Ultimately, Ayodhya symbolizes righteousness, morality, and immortality.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ayodhya, the sacred land of Rama, signifies the abode of peace and righteousness. It symbolizes the victory of dharma over adharma and the triumph of love and devotion. The name echoes the profound belief in the power of truth and justice, instilling serenity and hope in the hearts of its inhabitants.
